newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar, Exxon to start gas-to-liquid plant.
newsitem.headline: Qatar, Exxon to start gas-to-liquid plant.

text.p: Qatar said on Saturday it would soon sign a memorandum of understanding with the U.S. Exxon Corporation to set up a $1.2 billion gas-to-liquid conversion plant to produce synthetic crude oil from the North Field gas.

"Our studies have confirmed the feasibility of the project and we have reached an advanced stage in our negotiations about the project", said Minister of Energy and Industry Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah.
"A MoU will be signed soon," Attiyah told reporters.

Gas-to-liquid conversion process is a relatively new technology, known as AGC-21, patented by Exxon. It uses a special catalytic process to directly convert methane-rich gas into middle distillates, such as heating oil and diesel.

Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC) officials said synthetic oil is free of most of the impurities found in conventional oil. But its thermal efficiency is lower than that of crude oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG).

A QGPC official said Qatar was going ahead with the project on a "pilot" basis to complement its multibillion-dollar LNG projects to utilise its gas reserves -- the third largest in the world after Russia and Iran.

"One of the advantages of the synthetic gas oil vis-a-vis liquefied natural gas is that it can be easily sold in the world crude oil market without a long-term take-or-pay commitment, besides it can be transported by conventional oil tankers, instead of the costly cryogenic tankers needed for LNG," he added.
The project will use one billion cubic feet a day of North Field gas to produce around 100,000 barrels a day of synthetic oil, said the official.
